column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/gem-auto-bump.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHAT THIS FILE PINS. gem-auto-bump is a ONE-JOB workflow — `bump` — and that
# one job carries exactly one condition:
#     if: github.actor != 'github-actions[bot]'
# So the whole job-selection surface is a single equality test against a single
# literal actor name, and every row below is an arm of it. There is no `needs:`
# graph, no status function, no toggle input, and no second job to interleave
# with. That makes the table small; it does not make it pointless — `bump`
# PUSHES A COMMIT AND A TAG to the consumer's main branch, so the difference
# between "this job ran" and "this job skipped" is the difference between a
# release being cut and nothing happening, and both outcomes report SUCCESS.
# WHY IT EXISTS. On 2026-08-08 pleme-io/graphql-synthesizer ran the sibling
# cargo-auto-release, reported SUCCESS, bumped + tagged + pushed, and published
# nothing — its ship job was skipped by a condition that is entirely correct.
# A deliberate skip and a broken skip produce the same green tick, because
# nobody had written down which jobs must run for a given input. This file is
# that statement for gem-auto-bump.
#   `bump` PUSHES. It commits a version bump to `main` and pushes a tag, and
#   with a consumer-supplied BOT_PAT that tag push is what TRIGGERS the gem
#   release workflow — i.e. this job is the first domino of a public RubyGems
#   publish. It is outward-facing and effectively irreversible (a yank does not
#   un-publish a gem version).
#   Row 1 is the intended DO-IT case: a human (or any non-bot actor) pushed to
#   main, so the gem bumps.
#   Row 2 is the DON'T-DO-IT case, and it is the load-bearing one: the actor is
#   `github-actions[bot]`, which is precisely the actor this workflow's own
#   bump commit pushes as. Without that skip the workflow re-triggers on its
#   own push and bumps forever. Row 2 pins the loop guard. Delete the `if:` and
#   row 2 goes red before an infinite bump loop reaches a consumer.
# ── WHAT THE ROWS DELIBERATELY DO NOT COVER, stated so nobody reads the green
#   EVERYTHING BELOW THE JOB IS INVISIBLE HERE. The real decision this
#   workflow makes — "did anything under lib/ or the gemspec change since the
#   last tag?" — lives in the `changes` STEP (`steps.changes.outputs.skip`) and
#   gates the three steps that actually bump, push and tag. This linter models
#   JOB selection only; step-level `if:` is below its resolution entirely. So
#   "bump ran" in this table means "the job was selected", NEVER "a version was
#   bumped" or "a tag was pushed". A repo whose only change was a README edit
#   selects `bump` here and then does nothing inside it, correctly. That gap is
#   not closable at this layer; it needs a step-level oracle or a test of the
#   `changes` script itself.
#   BOT_PAT IS NOT A SELECTOR. The optional `BOT_PAT` secret changes WHICH
#   token checkout and push use (and therefore whether the tag push triggers
#   the downstream release workflow), but no `if:` in this file reads it, so
#   there is no honest job-selection assertion to make about it. Modelling it
#   as a case key would read as coverage and be none.
#   `inputs.bump-type` IS NOT A SELECTOR EITHER. It is forwarded to
#   substrate-bump as a `with:` value; no condition reads it.
# ── THE PRIVACY KEY IS A TRIPWIRE, NOT AN ASSERTION ──────────────────────────
#   `github.event.repository.private` appears exactly once in this workflow and
#   it is in `runs-on` — it selects a billing label
#   (the self-hosted pool for private callers, `ubuntu-latest` for
#   public), not a job. No `if:` reads it today, so rows 1 and 3 select
#   identically. It is declared in every case ON PURPOSE: the day someone adds
#   `&& !github.event.repository.private` to the job condition — the exact edit
#   shape that made graphql-synthesizer ship nothing while reporting success —
#   row 3 turns red with NOT-RUN and the posture has to be written down rather
#   than acquired silently. Today it costs nothing and asserts nothing; it is
#   here so that tomorrow it does.
# 1. DO-IT. A human pushed to main; the gem bumps, commits, tags and pushes.
#    This is the only intended path to a release.
human-push-bumps
# 2. DON'T-DO-IT / THE LOOP GUARD. `bump` pushes its own commit as
#    github-actions[bot]; if that push re-selected this job the workflow would
#    bump forever. This row is the reason the `if:` exists — it must stay red
#    if the guard is ever removed or its literal actor name changed.
bot-push-is-the-loop-guard
# 3. TRIPWIRE ROW (see header). A PRIVATE consumer: privacy only picks the
#    runner label, so selection is identical to row 1. If this row ever
#    disagrees with row 1, a privacy gate was added to the job condition and
#    that decision must be stated here.
private-repo-still-bumps
# 4. A DIFFERENT bot. The guard names ONE literal actor, so any other bot
#    identity — dependabot, a renovate app, a PAT-authenticated bot account —
#    still selects `bump` and still cuts a release. That is the workflow's
#    actual behaviour, pinned here as a FINDING rather than left to be
#    discovered by a dependabot push tagging a gem. Widening the guard to all
#    bots is a real design change; it turns this row red, which is correct.
other-bot-actor-still-bumps
# 5. Actor present but EMPTY — the "the field was resolved and produced
#    nothing" state, distinct from any named actor. Empty != the bot literal,
#    so `bump` is selected. Asserted separately so that if the guard is ever
#    weakened to a truthiness test (`if: github.actor`), '' and 'drzzln' part
#    ways and this row catches it while row 1 stays green.
empty-actor-still-bumps
